gloss: inevitably; necessarily; as a natural consequence

definitions.gloss: inevitably; necessarily; as a natural consequence
definitions.explanation: Something that happens as a logical or unavoidable result of circumstances. Indicates that an outcome was bound to occur given the conditions.

examples.japanese: {必然的|ひつぜんてき}にそうなる。
examples.english: It will inevitably turn out that way.

examples.japanese: {人口|じんこう}が{増|ふ}えれば、{必然的|ひつぜんてき}に{食料|しょくりょう}の{需要|じゅよう}も{増|ふ}える。
examples.english: If the population increases, the demand for food will inevitably increase as well.

examples.japanese: グローバル{化|か}が{進|すす}めば、{必然的|ひつぜんてき}に{異文化|いぶんか}との{接触|せっしょく}が{増|ふ}えていく。
examples.english: As globalization advances, contact with different cultures inevitably increases.

notes:
USAGE:
{必然|ひつぜん} means "inevitability" or "necessity" and {的|てき}に makes it an adverb. Used in logical arguments, analysis, and formal writing to describe outcomes that follow naturally from given conditions. More formal and analytical than {必|かなら}ず (certainly, always).

The na-adjective form {必然的|ひつぜんてき}な is also common: {必然的|ひつぜんてき}な{結果|けっか} (an inevitable result).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {必然的|ひつぜんてき}に{生|う}まれる (to arise inevitably)
- {必然的|ひつぜんてき}な{結果|けっか} (an inevitable result)
- {必然的|ひつぜんてき}な{流|なが}れ (an inevitable trend)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {必|かなら}ず: certainly, always — more everyday, less analytical
- {当然|とうぜん}: naturally, of course — implies something is expected or obvious
- {不可避|ふかひ}: unavoidable — a more formal noun/na-adjective
